sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: pg_org_start
toolsAdded.description: Start a PiGroups organisation and make this session its root. This tool exists only in a session that has no identity yet: a session started with PIGROUPS_URL and PIGROUPS_TOKEN already belongs to a platform, so it is not given this tool at all. It finds the platform checkout (`platform_dir`, else PIGROUPS_PLATFORM_DIR, else ../PiGroups next to the adapter, else ../../PiGroups) and verifies it by src/main.ts; a failed lookup lists every candidate it tried. If <adapter dir>/org.json records a healthy organisation it reattaches to that one instead of starting a second platform. Otherwise it starts the platform detached (the organisation outlives this session), waits for /v1/health, bootstraps a root and writes org.json. Idempotent: a second call, from this session or a later one, reattaches. After success the member tools (pg_say, pg_members, pg_spawn, ...) appear and this session is the root; if it fails, the platform it started is stopped again.

name.description: Name for the root member (the organisation’s first name).

port.description: Local port for the platform; a free port by default.

data_dir.description: Where the platform keeps its database and log. Defaults to <adapter dir>/platform-data; reuse the recorded one when the platform process is gone but its organisation should return.

platform_dir.description: PiGroups checkout containing src/main.ts. Overrides PIGROUPS_PLATFORM_DIR and the defaults.

content.text: Call the pg_org_start tool exactly once with name="probe-root". Do not pass platform_dir or any other argument. Do not call any other tool. Then report its JSON result verbatim and stop.
I'll call the tool once as instructed.

toolsAdded.name: pg_members
toolsAdded.description: The live roster: id, name, parent_id, parent_name, relation (self|parent|child|sibling|peer), child_count and last_seen_at for every living member. `query` is a case-insensitive substring over the name — names are the only handle; ids are opaque. `total` is the roster size before filtering and `matched` is the number of rows returned, so `total: 23, matched: 0` means the query missed, not that nobody exists. `last_seen_at` is the last time that member authenticated — NOT liveness (the roster already lists only living members). Only a `child` can be aborted; a `peer` can only be messaged.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the member name.

toolsAdded.name: pg_say
toolsAdded.description: Send a message to a group (`g:<owner>`) or to a member id. Clears the owed reply for that conversation.

toolsAdded.name: pg_children
toolsAdded.description: Telemetry snapshot of this member’s direct children (state, since, tool, count) including what each one’s last round did (last assistant text and last tool call).

toolsAdded.name: pg_inspect
toolsAdded.description: Ask a member (usually a direct child) for its current phase, tool, owed replies, children, and its last round: the last assistant text and the last tool call (name, args preview, ok).

toolsAdded.name: pg_abort
toolsAdded.description: Send pg.abort to a member, or cut this session’s own running turn when no member is given.

member.description: Member id; omit to abort yourself.

toolsAdded.name: pg_schedule
toolsAdded.description: Wake this member once, `after_seconds` from now (at least 5 s, at most 24 h): the adapter delivers `[scheduled] note` and starts a turn. One-shot, never periodic. At most 8 wakes may be pending; the 9th is rejected. In memory only — a restart drops every pending wake. It does not bypass the delivery window, so the wake may arrive up to one window after the delay.

note.description: The line to deliver, prefixed with `[scheduled]`.

toolsAdded.name: pg_read
toolsAdded.description: Read conversation history backwards, e.g. to backfill a gap or re-read the briefing.

toolsAdded.name: pg_spawn
toolsAdded.description: Create a child member, send it the brief as a direct message, and start it in a new herdr pane. `args` is a raw pi argv tail for this one child: appended to the configured spawn command in order, not validated or rewritten by the adapter, so the caller decides how pi starts (including flags that change its mode). Do not guess pi flags from this schema; when a flag is unknown, run `pi --help` and read pi’s own manual.

brief.description: Task brief, sent as the first direct message.

args.description: Raw pi argv appended after the base command, in order, one array element per argv word (e.g. ["--model", "vendor/model"]). Not sanitised: a caller can pass `-p` or `--` and change how the child starts. `pi --help` lists the flags.

toolsAdded.name: pg_terminate
toolsAdded.description: Delete a child subtree (`DELETE /v1/members/{id}`); the platform cascades.

toolsAdded.name: pg_whoami
toolsAdded.description: Platform coordinates plus this adapter’s own state (owed conversations and nudge counts).
